2	  "title": "feat(workspaces): part 4 — per-workspace cloud, Assign to workspace, synced-folder safety (NIW2-602)",
3	  "body": "## Summary

Part 4 of several workspaces: Kaipu Cloud per workspace, "Assign to workspace…", and safety for workspace folders inside Google Drive, OneDrive or iCloud Drive.

- Linear: [NIW2-602](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-602) (part 4) and [NIW2-577](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-577) (drag-out hard links rename or unsync items in a Google Drive library).
- **Stacked on #482** (part 3, NIW2-601), which is stacked on #479 → #478. Base: `feature/niw2-601-workspaces-part-3-settings`. The latest part-3 head (`543053c4`) is merged in.
- Spec: `specs/2026-10-29-several-workspaces-design.md`. The orphan rule as built, the deploy order and what part 4 leaves out are now written in its "Cloud: server and client" and "Synced folders" sections.

## Server

- `cloud_asset.workspace_id`: nullable `text`, no foreign key, no rewrite of existing rows. Migration `0003_cloud_asset_workspace_id.sql` is one `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN`.
- `POST /assets/upload-intents` takes an optional `workspaceId`. A re-upload without one keeps the asset's current workspace, and an older desktop that sends none is still accepted.
- `GET /assets` and every asset summary include `workspaceId`.
- `PUT /assets/{assetId}/workspace` with `{ workspaceId: string | null }`: owner-only (another account's asset answers 404), validated (a plain id, max 64 chars, or `null` to unassign), idempotent.

**About the migration file.** On `main`, schema changes still ship with `db:push` (`commands.md`). Committed migrations exist only in the open #364 (ADR 0029, Proposed), so I generated this migration with `drizzle-kit generate` on top of #364's chain, offline, as `0003`. The journal here lists `0000`–`0003`; whichever of #364 and this PR merges second resolves `meta/_journal.json` to the four-entry version. Until #364 lands, the column goes out with `db:push`. No migration was run against any database.

## Desktop

**Cloud filter.** This replaces the part-1 stopgap (`ownsLegacyCloud`). The Library composes with a view of the catalog filtered to the active workspace; the cache file keeps every workspace's entries, and `lastSeenLocalId` updates merge into it inside the cache's write chain (`CatalogCache.update`). The rule, in `main/cloud/workspace-filter.ts`:

1. An entry's workspace is the server's `workspaceId`; an assignment still owed to the server wins over it.
2. The active workspace lists its own entries, plus the cloud copy of any of its local items.
3. Unassigned entries (`workspace_id = null`) show in the migrated Default workspace **until the user's first "Assign to workspace…"**, so nothing disappears on upgrade. After that first assignment they show only under Cloud → "Unassigned cloud items".
4. Entries of a workspace not registered on this Mac show in no Library, only in that list. Nothing is assigned automatically.

**Moves.** After a move commits, its cloud asset gets `PUT …/workspace` through a persisted retry queue (`userData/cloud-assign-queue.json`, backoff from 30 s to 1 h, also flushed after a catalog refresh). It never blocks or fails the move. Until the server confirms, the owed assignment overlays the catalog, so an offline move never shows the item in its old workspace.

**Uploads.** The desktop upload flow (NIW2-214) has not shipped, so no upload calls the server today. `main/cloud/upload-intent-client.ts` is the request that flow will use; its type makes `workspaceId` required.

**Cloud page → "This workspace".** Shows where the folder lives (This Mac, an external drive, or the detected provider), which Kaipu Cloud items its Library lists, and the unassigned cloud items with "Assign to workspace…" and "Assign all to workspace…".

**Synced folders** (decision 15, NIW2-577):
- **Detection:** by path after `realpath` (`~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-…`, `OneDrive…`, `~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs`), plus Google Drive's xattr `com.google.drivefs.item-id#S` on `identity.json`. Each step is bounded at 2 s. The provider is named on the Cloud page, in the switcher and on the Settings → Workspaces row.
- **Scratch files:** recording staging, move staging and drag copies go to `userData/workspace-scratch/<id>/`, never `.kaipu/tmp/` or `.kaipu/drag/`. The startup and quit sweeps cover them.
- **No hard links:** drag copies are real copies, and takes are placed by `rename`, not `link()`. A move with a synced side copies, verifies sha256 **at the final path**, then deletes, even when `stat.dev` matches (the "Move to" menu says "Synced folder · copies").
- **Evicted files:** detected by `SF_DATALESS` from one `/usr/bin/stat -f '%f %N'` call per listing. Zero blocks is only a fallback when that call returns nothing. An evicted file gets no thumbnail URL, `kaipu-media://` answers 409 without opening a stream, the orphan heal skips it, and it cannot be dragged or moved ("In the cloud: download it first").
- **Availability probe:** bounded at 5 s and never lists the provider root. A probe that does not answer while `stat` still sees the folder leaves the workspace available but "unverified": nothing can be moved into it until a later probe answers.

**Did the move's same-volume path hit the hard-link problem?** Yes. Part 2 linked the media and the companion files whenever `stat.dev` matched, and on the internal drive it always matches. A synced side now always takes the copy+verify path, staged in userData, placed by rename into a synced target. Tests cover a synced source, target and both, a mismatch at the final path, and a crash healed from the scratch folder.

findings.body:
`relocateFolder` calls `relocateWorkspace` (line 751), which for the active workspace runs `relocateActive` (relocate.ts:48). That commits the gate and calls `afterCommit` (switch-transaction.ts:135-137), and `afterCommit` broadcasts `workspacesChanged` and `library:changed` (index.ts:524-530). Only after that returns does line 755 run `syncStates.refresh(current)`. So the re-list in those broadcasts sees the new folder through the path rule alone (`SyncStates.of`, sync-state.ts:26-29), not the detection.

The siblings do it the other way round. `addWorkspace` refreshes at index.ts:578 and `createWorkspace` at index.ts:630, both before `runSwitch` commits.

For a folder under `~/Library/CloudStorage` or iCloud the path rule is right and nothing is lost. For a Drive folder outside those roots, detected only by the xattr (synced-folder.ts:85-91), the path rule answers null until the detection finishes. That detection can take up to about 4 s, since `realpath` and the xattr check are each bounded at 2 s (synced-folder.ts:80, 86-90). In that gap the gate is open, so `currentVault()` builds a `LibraryVault` with a null eviction probe (library/index.ts:74), and `syncedStagingFor` returns null (index.ts:393-399), so a take started then is staged in `.kaipu/tmp/` inside the synced folder. That is the case decision 15 keeps out of synced folders. The switcher also shows no provider until the final broadcast at line 759 corrects it.

Fix: detect the picked path before the transaction, as `addWorkspace` does, e.g. `await syncStates.refresh({ id, path: chosen })` after the picker and before `relocateWorkspace`. `SyncStates.of` only trusts a detection whose path matches the entry's current path (sync-state.ts:28), so a refused relocation leaves nothing wrong behind.
